properties.statement:
THE UNEXPORTED-WORK NUDGE WAS COMPUTED PER FILE AND STATED PER SEAT, AND ON A SEAT WITH MORE THAN ONE TARGET THE SENTENCE WAS FALSE. `loop_status.next` returned 8 lines on reflow2's own graph, 5 of them sync lines, each saying between 185 and 825 node(s) 'have never been exported'. Every one of those five named a one-off scratch dump under /tmp from a dead session. The committed record, docs/design/reflow2.json, held 3662 of 3662 live nodes, was `in_step`, and contributed NO line at all.

⭐ THE FRAMING THAT OPENED THE INVESTIGATION WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. The report said 'the single true line sits buried among them' — a signal-to-noise problem. There was no true line. Signal to noise was 0:5. Not one node was unexported, so all five sentences were untrue, and 'noisy' would have led to a ranking or filtering fix that left every sentence just as false.

MEASURED, and this is the step that settled it: a set difference of the worst line's target (probe-authority.json, 2837 nodes, claiming 825 unexported) against the committed export put ALL 825 of those node ids inside the committed export, with 0 nodes in the scratch file and absent from the record. The claim 'have never been exported' was refuted node for node.

⭐ THE CAUSE IS A SCOPE ERROR, NOT ACCUMULATION. `coherence.rs` ran `debts.iter().filter(|d| d.live_nodes > d.export_nodes).map(|d| d.message())` — a comparison against ONE FILE — and `SyncDebt::message()` then phrased the result as a fact about the GRAPH. 'Are these nodes exported' is a question about the SEAT, answered by the union of the records it keeps; asking it of each record separately multiplies one fact by however many records have fallen behind, and every copy asserts something the durable record disproves.

🛑 THE OBVIOUS FIX IS ALREADY REFUTED ON THIS EXACT CODE. All five paths were under /tmp, which makes 'stop tracking scratch paths' look like the cause — it is also what the report proposed ('nothing ever forgets one'). `chg:the-orientation-call-stops-rereading-stale-records` (2026-08-24) SHIPPED that rule and reverted it: fifteen tests in `the_record_moved_and_the_session_is_told` failed and were right to, because a hermetic test, a CI workspace and a container all put GENUINE shared records under a temp dir, one of them named 'the case the whole thing exists for'. And it would not have worked: this seat also tracks /home/ajs7/reflow2-backups/reflow2-2026-08-06-session-backup.json, 1545 nodes, on no temp path, which produces the identical false sentence the moment it enters the freshest six. Accumulation decides WHICH files speak. The scope error is why what they say is false.

⭐ THE CLASS: a per-item computation phrased as a whole-system fact, where every test exercised exactly ONE item so the two scopes were indistinguishable. All 21 tests in this file used a single target; the served surface routinely has six. A fix that only stopped today's five lines is a trigger fix — the class is 'the test fixture had one of the thing the field has many of'.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other served rollups phrase per-target findings as seat-wide claims (only this one was examined); and the three standing bounds on the node-count comparison are unchanged — equal counts with different ids, an edge-only divergence, and a property-only write remain invisible, so this is a reading aid and not a durability guarantee.
